title: Latency tail mitigation for quantized model serving
author: Marco Nguyen
content:
Summary:
This runbook describes an operational playbook to detect, mitigate, and post‑mortem quantization-related latency tail events (intermittent P99 spikes) for Redwood serving clusters. It focuses on latency characteristics introduced by lower-precision kernels, KV/cache interactions, and quantization-induced scheduling jitter.

Audience and scope:
- Intended audience: SREs on model-serving oncall, runtime engineers, and incident commanders.
- Applies to: Redwood Dedicated and Hosted inference pools running 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants (q4/q5) and mixed-precision fallbacks.
- Out of scope: model accuracy regressions (handled by evaluation/QA), customer prompt-level correctness investigations.

Why this exists:
Quantized execution reduces cost but can produce non-linear latency tails due to kernel variance, memory paging, and dynamic kernel selection. These tails can burn error budgets quickly for latency SLOs (example: 99th percentile > 2x target). This playbook gives prioritized, low-risk mitigations to restore SLOs while preserving throughput.

SLOs and thresholds referenced:
- SLO (Latency-critical): p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms (99.9th < 1s).
- Alert conditions (examples):
  1) p99 > 400ms for 5m -> pager (sev-2)
  2) p99 > 700ms for 3m OR sustained p99 > 600ms for 15m -> pager (sev-1)
  3) Error budget burn rate > 5x for 30m -> page and runbook escalation

Key telemetry and PromQL snippets:
- p99 latency (example):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster, model))
- gpu memory pressure (per node):
  avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_memory_total_bytes - nvidia_gpu_memory_free_bytes[2m]) / avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_memory_total_bytes[2m])
- KV cache hit-rate (prefix cache):
  sum(rate(prefix_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(prefix_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- quantized-kernel-fallbacks (custom):
  sum(rate(runtime_quant_kernel_fallbacks_total[5m])) by (kernel, node)
